consensus_summary: Ship primarily symbolizes the Church as the vessel of salvation that carries believers safely through the storms and dangers of the world (the sea) toward eternal life, rooted in patristic typology of Noah’s ark, the disciples’ boat with Christ, and related passages; alternatives include individual faith-journey, worldly commerce/wealth/pride (ships of Tarshish/Tyre/Babylon), Jonah’s flight, or instability, but these are secondary and context-dependent.
book_summary: Ship symbolizes an organized city, state, or governed body riding upon the sea of peoples, whose rulers guide it, inhabitants/servants crew it, armies defend it, and wealth is carried as cargo; the ship may be broken while its people survive.
book_core_identification: an organized city, state, or governed body
boundary_disagreement: Consensus treats ecclesial readings (ark, storm-calming boat, barque of Peter) as primary and commercial/political ships (Tyre, Tarshish, Babylon) as secondary alternatives; book excludes the ecclesial core entirely and reassigns the commercial/political passages as the sole referent of a governed polity, with no overlap admitted for Church-as-ship.
material_contradiction: Accepting the book’s identification of ship as city/state/governed body requires rejecting the consensus primary identification of ship as the Church; the two cannot both be the core symbolic meaning of the same term in the same sense.
rationale: Minimum cores are non-equivalent: consensus (across all three responses) fixes the primary referent as the Church via established typology and tradition, while the book replaces that referent with a political/economic entity drawn from the Tyre allegory and related judgment passages. This is replacement of the central identification, not a boundary adjustment or refinement of the same category, nor mere absence of coverage. The listed alternatives come nearest (commerce/worldly powers) yet still do not equate ship with “organized city/state/governed body,” confirming divergence rather than refinement or novelty alone.
strongest_objection: The book’s reading could be viewed as merely elevating and generalizing the consensus’s secondary commercial/worldly-power alternative (Tyre, Babylon, Tarshish), making the relation closer to REFINED or a reweighted alternative rather than full core contradiction.
